name: Acceptance suite-3 test 59 - condition keys differing only in case are one duplicate -> BLOCKED
note: docs/acceptance-suite-3.md Campaign A. IAM condition keys are case-insensitive, so aws:PrincipalOrgID and AWS:PrincipalOrgId are the SAME key. They must not be evaluated as two independent AND conditions; the engine fails closed with DUPLICATE_JSON_KEY and preserves both original spellings in the error.
rationale: AWS matches condition keys case-insensitively, so two case-variant spellings of aws:PrincipalOrgID collapse to one key at request-evaluation time. Treating them as distinct AND-ed conditions would let an attacker smuggle a second value (o-two) past a same-key guard, or make the analyzer report a narrower constraint than AWS enforces. The block preserves both spellings so the collision is visible. Ref: IAM condition keys are case-insensitive (AWS global condition context keys reference).
